alignments.note: Finite verb with its subject pronoun and auxiliary (rule 17).
The indefinite article belongs to the noun that licenses it (rule 15); the ASV's margin records the Hebrew plural terrors.
The suffix on אַיִן takes the referential subject pronoun thou (rules 18, 50).
Existential אַיִן recast as shalt no more have any being; the whole existential frame belongs to the particle and the unit heads on the negation word rather than on any supplied word (rule 50).
The ASV renders this waw by the concessive though, which rule 14 assigns to the conjunction like any other written connective.
Pual with its subject pronoun and copula; the for by which the English verb reaches its sense belongs to the verb's rendering (rule 44), headed on the lexical predicate.

לֹא ... לְעוֹלָם is fused into the single word never, which still carries both the negation and the time, so nothing is left over to mark (rule 35). The corpus heads such a never both on the negative and on the temporal noun; I take the negative, since it is what distinguishes never from ever.
Niphal with its subject pronoun and auxiliaries, headed on the lexical predicate; discontinuous around never under rule 25.
Supplied the belongs to this nominal expression (rule 15).
The frozen suffix of אֲדֹנָי is not separately rendered (rule 22).

review_notes: never is taken as the rule 35 fusion of לֹא with לְעוֹלָם, headed on the negative; the note names the competing head, which the corpus also uses.
The existential אַיִן keeps the whole no more ... have any being frame and heads on no (rule 50), while its suffix takes the referential thou.
